### Explanation
There are 6 Millennium Prize Questions. My probability that AI will contribute to a correct proof of at least one of them is nearly certain. For 2050 I give a 90% chance of at least one proof. The probability of that outcome is roughly the complement of the probability that AI will not contribute to a proof of any of the questions by 2050, so this implies that I estimate the probability of AI not contributing to a proof of any by 2050 is about 10%.
For 2040 I estimate the chance of at least one proof as 0.8. The probability of that outcome is analogous to the above: roughly the complement of the probability of no proof by 2040.
The probabilities for 2026, 2030, and 2035 are based on extrapolating the particular assumptions I am making that AI will eventually attain human capabilities in mathematics but it will take many years or decades to do so.
